_note: The Go/No-Go rules' figures and boundaries, written down from the Aviation Weather Handbook, 14 CFR 91.103, 91.133 and 91.137-91.145, the AIM and the PHAK, never from the code. Shape and checks as engine/facade/tests/common/cases.rs says; asked by engine/facade/tests/rule_cases.rs.

cases.name: 6,000 ft flown over a 5,000 ft freezing level in the moisture: icing possible
cases.source: FAA-H-8083-28B (Aviation Weather Handbook) ch. 20: structural icing needs visible moisture at a temperature at or below 0 C, so an altitude at or above the freezing level, in the moisture, may ice; one below it does not. A PIREP of NEG icing reports none (AIM 7-1-20).

cases.name: A TFR of 16:00 to 18:00Z, the flight there An hour before: before
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.137-91.145: a TFR binds from its effective to its expiry time; the rule widens that by its own margin, 30 minutes either side, so a flight near its edges is told of it (the safer side); one with no times is in force.

cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103: the pilot's own minimums are the pilot's; a figure under one is said, one at it is not (FAA-H-8083-2A, Risk Management Handbook, ch. 3, personal minimums).

cases.name: Adverse conditions: the crossed TFR and the Convective SIGMET stop, then the CWA; the AIRMET one more
cases.source: AIM 7-1-5(b)(1): a standard briefing gives first the adverse conditions, "significant meteorological and/or aeronautical information that might influence the pilot to alter or cancel the proposed flight": a TFR the route crosses (14 CFR 91.137-91.145) and a Convective SIGMET or SIGMET (AIM 7-1-6) before a CWA, an urgent PIREP (UUA, AIM 7-1-18) or an AIRMET. A routine PIREP, a TFR only near the route and a SIGMET over before the flight are not adverse conditions on it.

cases.name: Runway findings: each field named once, in the route's order, under each flag it has
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): "For any flight, runway lengths at airports of intended use, and ... takeoff and landing distance information"; the checks' flags are gonogo_runway_checks' (over the runway, past the POH's table, past its demonstrated crosswind, under SAFO 19001's 15 per cent to spare, the length or elevation not known). No temperature reported: the distances are a standard day's, shorter than a hot day's (FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11, density altitude), named only where distances were worked out.

cases.name: Runway findings: calm along the end is no tailwind, half a knot behind is
cases.source: AIM 4-3-6: the runway most nearly into the wind; a wind along the end below zero is behind the airplane (gonogo_runway_checks' headwind_kt, negative for a tailwind).

cases.name: Runway findings: a length not known leaves the field unchecked; an empty reason does not
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): with no runway length, whether the distances fit is not known, never "within".

cases.name: Runway findings: awaiting the nav log, pending and not held unworked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): "For any flight, runway lengths at airports of intended use, and ... takeoff and landing distance information"; the checks' flags are gonogo_runway_checks' (over the runway, past the POH's table, past its demonstrated crosswind, under SAFO 19001's 15 per cent to spare, the length or elevation not known).

cases.name: Runway findings: an empty takeoff table {} is not worked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): the pilot is to become familiar with "takeoff and landing distance information"; an empty table holds none, so the distances were not worked from the POH (the planner's bool({}) was false).

cases.name: Runway findings: an empty landing table [] is not worked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): the pilot is to become familiar with "takeoff and landing distance information"; an empty table holds none, so the distances were not worked from the POH (the planner's bool({}) was false).

cases.name: Runway findings: a hollow takeoff table, its weights or grids empty, is not worked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): the pilot is to become familiar with "takeoff and landing distance information"; a table with no weights or no grid ({"tables": []}) holds no figure, so the distances were not worked from the POH.

cases.name: Runway findings: a takeoff table with grids but no weights is not worked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): the pilot is to become familiar with "takeoff and landing distance information"; a table with no weights or no grid ({"tables": []}) holds no figure, so the distances were not worked from the POH.

cases.name: Runway findings: awaiting the briefing, pending
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): "For any flight, runway lengths at airports of intended use, and ... takeoff and landing distance information"; the checks' flags are gonogo_runway_checks' (over the runway, past the POH's table, past its demonstrated crosswind, under SAFO 19001's 15 per cent to spare, the length or elevation not known).

cases.name: Runway findings: an airplane with no landing table is not worked
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b)(1): the distances are the airplane flight manual's; without its landing table they cannot be worked out.

cases.name: Go / No-Go input under IFR: VFR not recommended dropped, the sources, the forecast icing and a ceiling with no height unchecked, the worst forecast's visibility to the hundredth down
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.169: under IFR the weather checked is the destination's and the alternate's, not VFR's minimums (AIM 7-1-5's VFR flight not recommended); 14 CFR 91.103: all the available information, so a source not had or a ceiling with no height is not checked, never met; a visibility is never shown more than was seen (FMH-1's reportable values, down).

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: a plan's altitudes and name, the highest leg for oxygen, and a POH loading with no load is "give your load"
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.211(a): oxygen is asked of the highest altitude flown; 14 CFR 91.9(a) and the POH's section 6: the weight and balance is this flight's load against the limits, so with no load given it is not worked.

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: the pilot's own load balanced, "2,407 lb at 41.3 in"
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.9(a): the airplane flown within its POH's weight and balance limits; the takeoff's weight and centre of gravity as the row says them, the arm to a tenth (41.25 is 41.3, as JavaScript's toFixed).

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: with no nav log the altitude, the runways and the balance are pending
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103: each finding waits on what it is worked from, never reads clear before it is in.

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: a ceiling with no height at a field landed at and at TAF stations along the route, each once, unchecked
cases.source: 14 CFR 1.1, ceiling: "the height above the earth's surface of the lowest layer of clouds or obscuring phenomena that is reported as 'broken', 'overcast', or 'obscuration'"; with no height reported it is not known, and 14 CFR 91.103 asks the pilot to become familiar with "all available information": said unchecked, not met and not missed.

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: the winds aloft failed, so no legs: oxygen read from the plan picked's highest step
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.211(a): oxygen at cabin pressure altitudes above 12,500 ft MSL; the altitude planned is the plan's own where the winds aloft failed and no leg was flown out, and where no plan is picked the least any plan's highest step is, which every plan offered climbs to.

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: no legs and no plan picked: the least of the plans' highest steps
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.211(a): oxygen at cabin pressure altitudes above 12,500 ft MSL; the altitude planned is the plan's own where the winds aloft failed and no leg was flown out, and where no plan is picked the least any plan's highest step is, which every plan offered climbs to.

cases.name: Go / No-Go input: a pressurised cabin is said as one, not as oxygen carried
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.211(b)(1): a pressurised cabin's own oxygen rules, above FL250 a 10-minute supply for each occupant and above FL350 a pilot's mask, apply where (a)'s heights are the cabin's.
